questions.prompt: Net generation of energy on complete oxidation of a 15-carbon fatty acid is…..?
options: Equal to the energy generation from a 16-carbon fatty acid
Equal to the energy generation from a 14-carbon fatty acid
Less than the energy generation from a 14-carbon fatty acid
In between the energy generation from a 14-carbon fatty acid and an 16-carbon fatty acid
questions.note: C is correct: activation and propionyl-CoA carboxylation cost energy, and the final three-carbon fragment enters at succinyl-CoA rather than yielding another acetyl-CoA. Odd-chain C15 yields less net ATP than C14 under the stated complete-oxidation convention.

evidence: Biochemistry · Pharm.D · 23 June 2021 (IZAM), original question 23, source page 6.
Biochemistry II review, PDF p. 23: Lipolysis, carnitine transport and beta-oxidation.

questions.explanation: C is correct: activation and propionyl-CoA carboxylation cost energy, and the final three-carbon fragment enters at succinyl-CoA rather than yielding another acetyl-CoA. Odd-chain C15 yields less net ATP than C14 under the stated complete-oxidation convention.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is correct about liver enzymes?

In chronic cases, ALT is more elevated than AST.
ALT is more liver specific than AST.
In the mild hepatocellular damage: AST/ALT > 1
questions.note: Both A and C are defensible: ALT has a longer circulating half-life and is more liver-specific than AST. A blanket rule for all chronic liver disease is not valid; the AST/ALT ratio depends on etiology and stage.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about the long-term fasting is correct?
options: Adipose tissue can produce ketone bodies from its fat stores
The liver use ketone bodies to produce energy
Muscles produce ketone bodies from fatty acids
Muscles and brain use ketone bodies to produce energy
questions.note: Liver produces but does not oxidize ketone bodies. Brain adapts to their use; muscle can use them, although muscle increasingly relies on fatty acids during prolonged starvation.
